matt (acme-eng): Hey team — we're seeing streaming responses from the Redwood API drop after ~60s of silence. Client reconnects but gets partial output (truncated token stream). Happening for a subset of long responses where the model pauses for generation. Using Cloudflare in front of an ALB -> nginx -> app. Anyone seen this pattern?

ella (support): thanks — can you paste a minimal repro curl and any headers you see? Also did this start after any deploy?

matt (acme-eng): repro:
```
# direct to our ALB domain (via Cloudflare normally)
curl -v --http1.1 --no-buffer -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://api.acme.example/stream?prompt=long'
```
Output stops mid-event after ~61s. Verbose shows HTTP/2 200 then streaming bytes then connection closed by peer. No explicit error code in body. Our app logs show normal stream writes but then client closed. We tried client-side reconnect and resume, but the partial event header gets lost.

matt (acme-eng): quick verbose fragment:
```
< HTTP/2 200
< content-type: text/event-stream
< transfer-encoding: chunked

data: {"token":"hello"}

data: {"token":"world"}
# ...then silence for 61s while model decides next tokens...
# connection abruptly closed (client sees EOF)
```

ella (support): sounds like an idle timeout somewhere. Default ALB idle timeout = 60s. Cloudflare can also buffer or tear connections depending on settings. Do you have any heartbeat/keepalive from your app while model is quiet?

matt (acme-eng): we don't send heartbeats. We only flush when tokens are available. We assumed chunked transfer + SSE was enough.

deploy-bot: deploy "runtime/2026-11-09" succeeded 19m ago to prod (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:

kevin (infra): a couple quick pointers:
- ALB default idle timeout is 60s (can be increased): that will close the ALB->client connection if no bytes flow for that window.
- If Cloudflare (or a reverse proxy) sits in front, it may buffer responses until a threshold or it hits its own timeout. Cloudflare's "Response Buffering" / HTTP/2 behavior can delay chunk propagation.
- nginx between ALB and app: check proxy_read_timeout and proxy_buffering; nginx will buffer and may close upstream if backend stalls.

sarah (eng-runtime): adding details specific to SSE/chunked streaming:
- You need the full chain to flush chunks immediately: app must flush, nginx must be configured to pass through (proxy_buffering off, proxy_http_version 1.1, chunked_transfer_encoding on), ALB must allow long idles or there must be periodic bytes on the wire.
- Workarounds: send a lightweight heartbeat comment every ~15s (eg ":\n\n" or "data: \n\n") while generation stalls.

sarah (eng-runtime): nginx snippet that usually works for SSE: 
```
location /stream/ {
  proxy_pass http://backend;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";     # use keepalive to upstream
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  proxy_read_timeout 360s;             # allow long streams
  sendfile off;
}
```

sarah (eng-runtime): ALB guidance: if you control the ALB, bump the idle timeout to something > expected largest pause (eg 300s). NLB behaves differently and is more transparent but you might be using ALB for routing.

kevin (infra): Cloudflare notes: Cloudflare will buffer responses for certain plans/features (Workers, Argo, or some WAF/Polish settings). For SSE you usually want to bypass proxying buffering. Easiest test: bypass Cloudflare (direct DNS) and repro to ALB (curl with Host header) to see which layer drops.

matt (acme-eng): OK testing now — bypassed CF and hit ALB directly: still drops at ~60s. ALB access logs show connection_end_reason = IdleTimeout.

ella (support): that nails it -> ALB idle timeout. Two mitigations: 1) add heartbeat from app (quick), 2) increase ALB idle timeout (infra change). We'll propose both.

matt (acme-eng): can we also get config examples for the heartbeat? Don't want to send a full SSE event, just keepalive bytes.

sarah (eng-runtime): simplest is an SSE comment line every 10-15s: the SSE spec treats lines starting with ':' as comments and clients ignore them but they still cram bytes across proxies. Example server-side: 
```
// pseudo-code
while (not finished) {
  if (model_has_token) {
    write("data: {json}\\n\\n");
    flush();
  } else {
    // heartbeat
    write(": heartbeat\\n\\n");
    flush();
  }
  sleep(10s);
}
```

sarah (eng-runtime): also recommend using Transfer-Encoding: chunked and calling flush after every write. On many languages/frameworks you need to disable response buffering middleware.

kevin (infra): infra action items:
- temp: increase ALB idle timeout to 300s for this target group (we can revert later).
- config: verify nginx proxy_read_timeout and proxy_buffering match snippet above.
- test: run synthetic client that waits 2+ minutes between token emits.

matt (acme-eng): infra changed ALB idle timeout to 300s (thanks). Testing now.

matt (acme-eng): after ALB change, direct tests keep open beyond 60s. Still seeing occasional truncation when going through Cloudflare (dev plan) though.

ella (support): for Cloudflare path: try disabling any Cloudflare "Optimize" features and use a Page Rule to "Bypass cache" for the stream endpoint. If that still truncates, we may need to route SSE traffic through a separate subdomain that bypasses Cloudflare entirely.

matt (acme-eng): bypassed CF for stream subdomain — works reliably now. So root cause: Cloudflare buffering + ALB idle too; ALB fixed the 60s symptom, Cloudflare also needed bypass to avoid buffering.

sarah (eng-runtime): final recommendations (we should push to docs):
- Ensure every node in the chain supports immediate flush: client -> CF (or CDN) -> ALB -> nginx -> app.
- Add lightweight SSE heartbeats at ~10-15s when model pauses.
- Nginx: proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout large.
- ALB: bump idle timeout if you expect >60s stalls.
- For Cloudflare: either bypass for streaming endpoints or confirm plan/feature settings that disable response buffering.
